question: Bind, execute A Site via A Short 4v5, 58s. You are Raze entry (Boom Bot, 2 satchels, nade). How do you open the site on a disadvantaged push?

options.label: Send the Boom Bot into A Short/site to force DEF to reveal or back off, then satchel into the space it creates
options.explication_courte: The Boom Bot forces a reaction: DEF reveal their position (info) or back off (space gained). Satchel-swinging into known space is the correct entry sequence.

options.label: Nade (Paint Shells) the default A Short angle, then immediately satchel-swing into the opening
options.explication_courte: Clearing a likely angle with nade + fast satchel-swing is playable, but without the Boom Bot info you might satchel into an unknown position.

sources_option.citation: Raze can clear multiple angles with Paint Shells and Boom Bot before entering, reducing the number of angles she needs to worry about.

options.label: Double-satchel directly onto site without any info util for an ultra-fast surprise entry
options.explication_courte: Satchel entry with no info in a 4v5 exposes Raze to 5 unknown angles at once; speed does not substitute for information.

sources_option.citation: Clear one angle at a time; entering dry into a site without info exposes you to multiple sightlines simultaneously, worst in a man-down situation.

options.label: Wait in A Short for teammates to enter first and hold all Raze util for a potential clutch
options.explication_courte: Raze is the entry fragger: holding her offensive util in a 4v5 leaves teammates under-supported and wastes the Boom Bot entirely.

sources_option.citation: Your job as a duelist is to take space first; hoarding your entry utility means a worse-equipped teammate eats the opening duel.

explication_longue:
Situation: execute A Site Bind via A Short in 4v5 (one teammate down), 58 seconds, full-buy both sides. You are Raze, the entry, with Boom Bot, 2 Blast Packs (satchels) and Paint Shells (nade).

Entry in a 4v5 is about gathering intel before spending your body. The Boom Bot is the most underrated entry tool in Valorant: it forces defenders to react (reveal by shooting it, or back off and cede space). Once the Boom Bot does its job, you satchel into the created space - you are not entering blind.

Nading the default angle + satchel-swing (acceptable) works if defenders are predictable, but misses the Boom Bot intel value. Blind double-satchel (costly) trades speed for zero information: in a 4v5 with 5 unknown angles, dying first turns it into a 3v5. Holding all util (mistake) wastes the Boom Bot on a clutch that never comes.

Estimated elite distribution: ~55% Boom Bot info then satchel entry, ~22% nade+satchel-swing, ~16% blind double-satchel (costly), ~5% hold all util (mistake).

sources.citation: Raze can clear multiple angles with Paint Shells and Boom Bot before entering, reducing the number of angles she needs to worry about; take first contact.
Send a Boom Bot to force the defender to react; a critical entry skill is visualizing the optimal defense to prioritize which angles to clear.
Clear one angle at a time and use utility to force a reaction; entering dry against a numbers disadvantage exposes you to too many sightlines.

_gaps.incertitude: Le 4v5 suppose un teammate deja tombe en execute ; selon COMMENT il est tombe (info deja acquise ou non), la valeur du Boom Bot-info varie. Un juge pourrait ajuster si l'equipe a deja de l'info sur le setup.
Nade+satchel-swing pourrait etre juge 'optimal' par des Raze tres mecaniques qui clear a la nade avec un read fiable ; la separation optimal/acceptable est fine et depend du read.
Estimations depuis guides entry/duelist ; les frequences exactes en 4v5 execute varient fortement selon le style d'equipe (fast vs slow default) non specifie.
